sections.html: Dwarf shrimps are charming and completely harmless, but also very small. So keepers of somewhat larger fish often search for a species of shrimp which is absolutely harmless and day active, but also a bit larger – too large to be eaten as an intermediate snack between dinner and supper. For these cases mother nature has produced Atyoida pilipes. This shrimp attains a maximum length of about 5 cm.

This shrimp feeds exclusively on very small particles of food which are filtered with the fan-like shaped claws out of the water. The animals are completely harmless. In an aquarium they also feed readily on dry food for fishes, so feeding them is no problem at all. The best choice are food tablets that decay slowly in the water. Here all A. pilipes that live in the tank will meet quite fast.
This shrimp likes to live in larger aggregations, so one should never keep them alone. In any other respect the animal is absolutely undemanding.
Breeding A. pilipes is difficult: raising the very tiny larvae is quite difficult, because they develop only in marine environments.
